                        Introduction

   •  The Finance Commission (FC) is a Constitutional body constituted by the President every five years
        in pursuance to Article 280(1) of the Constitution to make recommendations on centre-state fiscal
        relations.
   •  About 16th FC:
       §  Chairman: Dr Arvind Panagariya (former Vice-Chairman, NITI Aayog)
       §  Mandate: Constituted to provide recommendations on centre-state fiscal relations for the
          period succeeding the 15th FC, which concluded on March 31, 2026.
       §  Recommendation Period: 5-years (2026-27 to 2030-31).


               Key Recommendations

Share of States in Central Taxes (Vertical Devolution)

   •   States' share in the divisible pool of central taxes recommended at 41% — same as recommended
      by the 15th Finance Commission.
   •   Divisible pool is arrived at after excluding cost of collection and cesses and surcharges from the
       gross tax revenue collected by the central government.
   •   Divisible Pool = Gross Tax Revenue of Centre minus cost of collection minus cesses and surcharges.


          Vertical devolution of the FC is the sharing of net central tax proceeds between the Union (Centre)
       and State governments, aimed at correcting fiscal imbalances. It determines the total percentage
         of tax revenue transferred from the centre to all states combined




Criteria for Devolution (Horizontal Devolution)



            •   Horizontal devolution of the Finance Commission is the process of distributing the
                  collective share of central taxes among individual Indian states, ensuring inter-state
                equity and addressing fiscal disparities.
            •    It determines each state's specific share from the total pool to balance developmental
                needs.

                                   Criteria Comparison: 15th FC vs 16th FC

                                 Criteria           15th FC (2021-26)     16th FC (2026-31)
                 Income Distance         45%             42.5%
                   Population (2011)        15%             17.5%
                 Demographic Performance  12.5%          10%
                  Area                  15%           10%
                    Forest                10%           10%
                   Tax and Fiscal Efforts       2.5%              Discontinued
                    Contribution to GDP    —             10% (New)
                      Total                  100%           100%

Key Changes & Definitions:

   •  Income Distance (42.5%): Defined as the difference between per capita GSDP of a state and the
       average per capita GSDP of the top 3 large states with the highest per capita GSDP.
       §  Computed as average over 2018-19 to 2023-24 (excluding pandemic year 2020-21).
       §   States with lower per capita GSDP get a higher share to maintain equity.
   •  Population (17.5%): Based on the 2011 Census data (weight increased from 15% to 17.5%).
   •  Demographic Performance (10%): Redefined from the 15th FC's TFR-based approach to now
      measure population growth between 1971 and 2011. States with lower population growth get a
       higher share.
   •  Forest (10%): 16th FC considers both the share in overall forest area and the increase in forest
      area between 2015 and 2023. It also includes open forests (unlike the 15th FC which counted only
      dense and moderately dense forests).
   •  Contribution to GDP (10%) — New Parameter: Replaces the Tax and Fiscal Efforts parameter.
       Calculated as the square root of a state's GSDP as a share of the sum of square roots of GSDP of all
        states. Based on average nominal GSDP between 2018-19 and 2023-24 (excluding 2020-21).

Grants-in-Aid

   •  The 16th FC has recommended grants worth Rs 9.47 lakh crore over the five-year period. These
      comprise grants for:
        1. Urban and rural local bodies
        2.  Disaster management.
   •  The 16th FC has discontinued the following grants recommended by the 15th FC:
        1. Revenue deficit grants
        2.  Sector-specific grants
        3.  State-specific grants

   •  Grants for local bodies: The 16th FC has recommended grants worth Rs 4.35 lakh crore and Rs 3.56
       lakh crore for rural and urban local bodies, respectively.
       §  These grants are divided into basic (80%) and performance-based (20%) components.
       §   Special Infrastructure Grants and Urbanisation Premium Grants have also been recommended
           for urban local bodies.
   •   All local body grants will be available upon fulfilment of three entry-level criteria:
        1.  Constitution of the local bodies as per the Constitution
        2.  Publication of provisional and audited accounts of the local bodies in the public domain
        3.  Timely constitution of the State Finance Commission.
   •  Basic grants: 50% of the basic grant will be untied and the rest 50% will be tied to:
        1.  Sanitation and solid waste management, and/or
        2.  water management.
   •  Performance Grants: Divided into
        1.  State Performance Grants: linked to minimum benchmark for transfers to local bodies from
        own resources.
        2.  Local Body Performance Grants: linked to own source revenue growth targets.
   •  Special infrastructure grants: This component will be tied to the development of a comprehensive
      wastewater management system in cities with population between 10-40 lakh as per the 2011
       census. Grants worth Rs 56,100 crore have been recommended over five years.
   •  Urbanisation premium grant (Rs.10,000 Crore): These will be released to states as a one-time grant
        for:
        1. Merger of peri-urban villages into adjoining urban local body areas and
        2.  Formulation of a Rural to Urban Transition Policy.

Disaster Management Grants:

   •  The 16th FC Commission has recommended disaster management corpus of Rs 2,04,401 crore (with
       Centre’s share of Rs 1,55,916 crore) for State Disaster Relief and Management Funds (SDRF and
      SDMF).
   •  The cost-sharing pattern between the centre and states is recommended to be:
        1.  90:10 for north-eastern and Himalayan states
        2.  75:25 for all other states



Fiscal Roadmap

   •  Centre's Fiscal Deficit to be brought down to 3.5% of GDP by 2030-31.
   •   States' annual fiscal deficit limit recommended at 3% of GSDP.
   •  Off-budget borrowings for States to be strictly discontinued and all such borrowings to be brought
       on-budget.
   •   Definition of fiscal deficit and debt to be expanded to uniformly include all off-budget
       borrowings.
   •  Combined debt (Centre and States) projected to decline from 77.3% of GDP in 2026-27 to 73.1% of
     GDP by 2030-31.


Power Sector Reforms

    •  States should actively pursue privatisation of electricity distribution companies (DISCOMs).
    •  Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) may be created to warehouse DISCOM debt and shielding private
        investors after discom-takeover.
    •  States may use funds from the Special Assistance Scheme for Capital Investment for pre-
       payment/repayment of DISCOM debt — but only after the privatisation process is complete.



Subsidy Expenditure Reforms

   •  States recommended to review and rationalise subsidy expenditure.
   •  Schemes with unconditional cash transfers tend to have large, untargeted beneficiaries — clear
       exclusion criteria and rigorous review processes recommended.
   •  Discontinuation of Off-budget borrowings for financing subsidies.
   •  Adoption of a uniform approach for accounting and disclosure of subsidies and transfers. At
       present, there is lack of standardisation in defining and accounting of subsidies and transfers across

        states. It observed that subsidies and transfers across states are being misclassified as assistance,
        grants, or other expenditure.

Public Sector Enterprise (PSE) Reforms

   •  Recommended review and closure of 308 inactive State Public Sector Enterprises (SPSEs).
   •  States should formulate a state-level PSE disinvestment policy targeting inactive and
      underperforming SPSEs.
   •  Any State or Union PSE incurring losses for 3 out of 4 consecutive years to be placed before the
       respective Cabinet for a decision on closure, privatisation, or continuation based on strategic
       importance.
